thread:
elaine: ok team — Q3 roadmap planning: need a short set of launch criteria for Dedicated autoscale lanes (isolation + burst). customers are pushing for predictable SLAs and burst billing model. thoughts?

tom: +1 on prioritizing predictable latency for reserved customers. main risk is noisy neighbors when bursts hit baseline. we need clear eviction/fallback rules. :thinking_face:

maria: SLO suggestion: 99.9% p50 latency under baseline load, 99.5% under burst scenarios for customer-tiered lanes. also: error budget policy for failover to hosted variants.

ajay: we should ship an autoscale policy that supports: `min_instances`, `reserved_capacity`, `burst_pool_pct`, `eviction_priority`. simple example:```yaml
policy:
  min_instances: 2
  reserved_capacity: 80%
  burst_pool_pct: 20
  eviction_priority: [best_effort, low_priority, reserved]
```
this is just a strawman.

neil: from sales/PLG: top customers want "burst credits" they can buy and a clear invoice line item. if burst billing is opaque, procurement will stall. also want an SLA doc they can send to security/compliance teams.

elaine: good. launch criteria draft (proposed):
- autoscale lanes feature gated behind customer tier flag
- documented SLA matrix + billing model for bursts
- telemetry: per-tenant burst usage, eviction events, queueing time
- fallback: automatic degrade to hosted model within 30s when reserved pool exhausted
- e2e tests + chaos scenario covering noisy neighbors
are we missing anything?

tom: add cost guardrails — must be able to set a hard budget per tenant so burst can't blow commits. also need an eviction simulation in staging to validate ordering.

maria: add alerting: if tail latency > SLA for >5m, create auto-rollout to fallback lane and page on-call. also track burst credit depletion as an alert.

ajay: implementation notes: runtime needs a fast path to decide routing: `if tenant.burst_credit > 0 and pool.available > 0 => route to burst_lane else route to reserved/hosted`. we can expose `burst_credit` as a simple integer in billing service.

neil: agree on billing. proposed pricing model: small monthly allowance + overage per 1k tokens. need to align with finance before commit.

elaine: oK. can we convert this into an OKR-friendly set of acceptance criteria? i.e., measurable checkboxes for the quarter.

tom: quick list:
- infra: autoscale lanes implemented + feature flag (dev->prod)
- reliability: fallback ON and validated in chaos tests (SLO met in 90% of simulated noisy neighbor windows)
- observability: burst metrics ingested and dashboards live + alerting rules
- billing: burst credits tracked and invoice line item rendered in billing UI
- docs: customer SLA + admin guide published

maria: target dates? we should aim for beta in 6 weeks, GA in 12 weeks if no major issues.

ajay: depends on kernel/placement work — if we get the scheduling heuristics in place, 6 weeks beta is tight but doable. need 2 engineers full-time for 4 weeks.

neil: i've queued two strategic customers for beta. they'll sign NDA but want access early. good for roadmap momentum. :rocket:

elaine: ok action items:
- tom/ajay: break down infra tasks and resource estimate by EOD Fri
- maria: draft SLO/SLA doc and alert playbook by next Wed
- neil: confirm billing pricing with finance and customers by next Tue
- i'll draft OKR acceptance criteria and share for signoff

deploy-bot: meeting created "Dedicated Autoscale Lanes: Roadmap sync" Thu 10:30am in #product-calendar

elaine: thanks — feel free to drop quick comments here. we will lock scope once infra estimates land. :thumbsup:
